translationRepairs: On the jiwei day, the Prince of Zheng Chonggui, Prince of Kaifeng and Administrator of the Kaifeng Prefecture; Liu Zhiyuan, Military Governor of the Guide Army and Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot; and Du Chongwei, Military Governor of the Zhongwu Army—all were promoted to Grand Councilor with the Concurrent Signatory of the Secretariat.

On the jiwei day, the imperial son Chonggui, Prince of Zheng and Administrator of Kaifeng; Liu Zhiyuan, Military Governor of the Guide Army and Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot; and Du Chongwei, Military Governor of the Zhongwu Army—all were promoted to Grand Councilor with the Concurrent Signatory of the Secretariat.
Chinese 開封尹 is the Kaifeng prefectural administrator office, not a second princely title “Prince of Kaifeng”; 皇子 goes with 重貴.
On the dingwei day, Long Min, deputy military commissioner of the Western Capital, was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
On the dingwei day, Long Min, deputy stay-behind commissioner of the Western Capital, was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
西京副留守 is the deputy capital stay-behind/guardian post, not a “deputy military commissioner.”
On the dingchou day, Wu Chengfang was transferred to secretariat drafter and made Hanlin academician;
On the dingchou day, Wu Chengfan was transferred to secretariat drafter and made Hanlin academician;
Chinese 吳承範 is Wu Chengfan (範 fàn); Chengfang misreads the given name.

On the jihai day, Lady Zhang, widow of the late Prince Chongying, took the tonsure as a nun; she was given the name Wushen and twenty summer fast days.
On the jihai day, Lady Zhang, widow of the late Prince Chongying, took the tonsure as a nun; she was given the name Wushen and twenty summers of monastic age.
夏臘 counts years since tonsure (monastic summers), not summer fast days.
On the jihai day, Lady Zhang, wife of the late Prince Chongying, shaved her head and became a nun; she was granted the name Wushen and also given twenty summer fast days.

僧尼 means Buddhist monks and nuns; the Chinese does not mention Daoists.
